A full groom can block your table for two hours or more. When a dog doesn't turn up, that time is lost, and it is rarely possible to fill it at short notice. Owners usually don't skip on purpose: the appointment was booked weeks ago, the day got busy, or the walk took longer than planned.

## Frequently asked questions

Can owners cancel by text?

Yes. Owners reply to confirm or cancel, or use the link in the text. Their answer appears on the appointment in your calendar.

Does it work for home visits?

Yes. Put the owner's address in the calendar event, and the appointment page shows it.

Do I need a new booking system?

No. Remind1 works with the Google Calendar or Outlook you already use. Keep booking as you do today and add the owner's phone number to the appointment.

Can the reminder say when to pick the dog up?

Yes. Add the end time of the appointment to your text, for example “Pick-up at 11:00”. Owners then know when to drop off and when to come back.

Does it work for dog training classes?

Yes. Weekly lessons entered as a recurring event get a reminder every time, so owners and their dogs don't miss a lesson.

Can I remind owners about regular grooming every few weeks?

Yes. Create the appointment as a recurring event in your calendar with the owner's phone number. Every appointment in the series gets its own reminder automatically.

Can the reminder say which pet it is for?

Yes. Put the pet's name and the service in the event title, for example “Bella – full groom”, and add the title to your reminder text. Owners with several pets know right away which appointment is meant.

# Writing Appointment Reminders That Actually Get Read

A reminder that gets ignored is as useless as no reminder at all. This guide covers the timing, tone, and wording that make clients actually read your messages — and turn up to their appointments.

![Smartphone showing a friendly dog grooming appointment reminder message](/assets/guide-sms-reminders-hero-Cq6bA2Ig.png)

## Why wording matters

Sending a reminder is only half the job. If it's confusing, impersonal, or buried in marketing waffle, clients skim past it. A good reminder is read in a glance, tells the client exactly what they need to know, and makes it effortless to act if something's changed. Get the wording right and the same reminder system works noticeably harder.

## What every reminder should contain

*   The client's name — so it reads as personal, not bulk
*   The dog's name — instantly recognisable and warm
*   The date and time, written clearly
*   Your salon name, so they know who it's from
*   A simple line on what to do if they need to change it

## Get the timing right

The sweet spot is **24 to 48 hours before** the appointment. Earlier than that and clients forget again; later and they may not have time to rearrange their day. Many salons use two touches: an email 48 hours out and an SMS 24 hours out.

With Pawfectly Booked you can set this timing once and it applies automatically to every appointment — anywhere from 1 to 72 hours before.

## Strike the right tone

Warm and brief beats formal and long. You're a local business that cares about their dog, not a faceless corporation. A friendly, human tone — using the dog's name — builds the relationship while doing the practical job of reminding them.

## Template examples

Here are reminder templates you can adapt. The bracketed parts are personalisation variables that fill in automatically.

SMS — 24 hours before

"Hi \[Client Name\]! Just a reminder that \[Pet Name\] is booked in with \[Salon Name\] tomorrow at \[Time\]. Looking forward to seeing you both. Need to change it? Just reply or call us."

Email — 48 hours before

"Hi \[Client Name\], this is a friendly reminder that \[Pet Name\]'s grooming appointment with \[Groomer Name\] is on \[Date\] at \[Time\]. If you need to reschedule, please let us know at least 24 hours in advance so we can offer the slot to another client. See you soon!"

SMS — booking confirmation

"Thanks \[Client Name\]! \[Pet Name\]'s appointment is confirmed for \[Date\] at \[Time\] with \[Salon Name\]. We'll send a reminder closer to the day."

## Personalise everything you can

Generic reminders feel like spam. Personalised ones feel like a note from someone who knows your dog. Using the client's name, the dog's name, and the groomer's name costs you nothing once your templates are set up — and it dramatically improves how the message lands.

## Let it run automatically

The best-written reminder in the world is useless if you forget to send it. Set your templates and timing once, and let the system send a perfectly worded, personalised reminder for every appointment — without you ever touching it again.

## Already booked vs due to book

This guide is about appointment reminders for clients who already have a booking. Active Standard and Gold subscriptions also include a separate marketing feature called Reminder to Book In, which can contact opted-in clients when their dog may be due or overdue for the next groom. Appointment reminders do not use Marketing Credits; Reminder to Book In does.

## Frequently asked questions

### What should a grooming reminder include?

The client's name, the dog's name, the date and time, your salon name, and a simple instruction for what to do if they need to change it. Keep it short, clear, and friendly.

### When is the best time to send a reminder?

24 to 48 hours before the appointment. This gives clients time to rearrange their day but keeps the appointment fresh. Some salons add a second reminder on the morning of the appointment.

### Should reminders be SMS or email?

Choose channels your clients use and have agreed to receive. Email can include more detail, while SMS provides a short prompt. Check plan availability, consent and message costs, and measure results rather than assuming one channel is always more effective.

### How do I personalise reminder messages?

Use variables that pull in the client's name, the dog's name, the appointment time, and the groomer's name. A personalised message is far more effective than a generic note.

### Can reminders reduce no-shows on their own?

Reminders can prompt a client, but they do not guarantee attendance. Consider them alongside clear booking and cancellation policies, and review your own salon’s results.

# Dog grooming text message templates

Updated November 3, 2026 · By the PawScheduler team

**Copy the texts below, change the \[brackets\], and save the ones you use most.** Keep each text short, put the date and time near the start, and always give a way to reply or reschedule. If you text clients from a business number, only text people who agreed to get texts, and include "Reply STOP to opt out" in reminders.

## Booking confirmation

Hi \[First name\]! \[Dog's name\] is booked with \[Business name\] on \[Day, Month Date\] at \[time\] for a \[service\]. Reply here if you need to change anything. See you then!

## Appointment reminder (1–2 days before)

Hi \[First name\], a reminder that \[Dog's name\] has a grooming appointment on \[Day\] at \[time\]. Reply C to confirm or call \[phone\] to reschedule. Reply STOP to opt out.

## Day-of reminder (mobile groomers)

Good morning! I'm on my way to you today for \[Dog's name\]. My window for you is \[time\]–\[time\]. Please have \[Dog's name\] ready and the parking spot clear. Reply if anything's changed!

## Running late

Hi \[First name\], I'm running about \[15\] minutes behind today. I'm sorry! New arrival time for \[Dog's name\] is about \[time\]. Reply if that doesn't work and we'll sort it out.

## Ready for pickup

\[Dog's name\] is all done and looking great! 🐾 Ready for pickup any time before \[time\]. Your total is $\[amount\].

## Rebook after the groom

Thanks for bringing \[Dog's name\] in today! For \[his/her\] coat, I recommend coming back in about \[6\] weeks. Want me to hold \[Day, Month Date\] at \[time\]? Reply YES and it's yours.

## Missed appointment (no-show)

Hi \[First name\], we missed \[Dog's name\] today at \[time\]. I hope everything is okay! As a reminder, our policy is \[policy\]. Reply here and I'll help you find a new time.

## Late cancellation

Thanks for letting me know, \[First name\]. Since this is within \[24\] hours, our \[late cancellation fee of $amount\] applies. I'd love to get \[Dog's name\] back on the books. Here's my next opening: \[Day\] at \[time\].

## Vaccine records request

Hi \[First name\], before \[Dog's name\]'s visit on \[Day\], could you send a photo of \[his/her\] current rabies certificate? Our records show it expired on \[date\]. Thank you!

## Price increase notice

Hi \[First name\], thank you for trusting me with \[Dog's name\]! Starting \[Month Date\], my prices are changing to keep up with supply and insurance costs. \[Dog's name\]'s \[service\] will be $\[new price\] (was $\[old price\]). Appointments already booked before then stay at the current price. Thank you for your support!

## Holiday booking

Holiday grooming spots are filling up! 🎄 If you'd like \[Dog's name\] looking sharp for the holidays, reply with a day that works and I'll save you a spot. Openings left: \[dates\].

## New client welcome

Welcome to \[Business name\], \[First name\]! Before \[Dog's name\]'s first visit, please fill out this quick form: \[link\]. It helps me get to know \[him/her\] and keep grooming safe. See you on \[Day\]!

## Tips for texting clients

*   **Get permission first.** Ask on your intake form or booking page, and keep a record of who said yes. Business texting rules in the US and Canada require consent.
*   **Text from a business number,** not your personal phone, so client texts don't get mixed into your family chats and you can stop work texts on your days off.
*   **Automate the repeat ones.** Confirmations and reminders are the same every time, so let your software send them. Keep personal texts for running late and pickups.
*   **Keep it short.** One screen, no long paragraphs. Date and time first.

PawScheduler sends confirmations and reminders automatically (email on Free and Basic, texts from your own business number on Growth), keeps a record of who agreed to texts, and has a two-way inbox for replies. See [how to reduce no-shows](https://pawscheduler.app/reduce-no-shows-dog-grooming) for when to send each reminder.

## Common questions

When should a dog groomer send appointment reminders?

A common setup is one reminder 24 to 48 hours before, and for mobile groomers a short message the morning of the appointment. Two reminders cut no-shows without annoying clients.

Do I need permission to text grooming clients?

Yes. For business texts in the US and Canada you need the client's consent, and reminders should include a way to opt out, like "Reply STOP to opt out". Ask on your intake form or booking page and keep a record.

Should I text clients from my personal phone?

It works when you're starting out, but a separate business number keeps work texts out of your personal messages, looks more professional, and lets you set up automatic reminders.

How do I tell grooming clients about a price increase?

Give at least 30 days' notice, keep the message short and thankful, say the new price and the date it starts, and keep already-booked appointments at the old price.

## Try it on your real schedule

The free plan covers up to 50 appointments a month. No credit card.

# Reducing Grooming No Shows with Text Message Appointment Reminders

Oct 11, 2019 | [Groomsoft](https://blog.groomsoft.com/category/groomsoft/)

![Text Message Appointment Reminder on iPhone](https://d13ddrtjxhzwjl.cloudfront.net/wp-content/uploads/2019/10/sms-appointment-reminder-replying-yes.png "Text Message Appointment Reminder on iPhone")

```

```

Americans have one of the [highest rates](https://www.pewinternet.org/fact-sheet/mobile/) of cell phone ownership in the world, 96% actually owning one and each household has at least 3. It is believed that currently 81% of these are smartphones.

Unfortunately, cell phone usage is one of the reasons for the high accident statistics on the roads and it is estimated that 1.6 million crashes, resulting in 390,000 injuries. In 2017, distracted driving [resulted in the death of](https://www.nhtsa.gov/risky-driving/distracted-driving) 3,166 people and all statistics show that texting is by far the most dangerous activity. It is 6 times more likely to cause an accident than driving drunk, according to insurance and law firms in the US.

[marketing experts](https://www.marketingprofs.com/chirp/2017/33045/email-vs-sms-battle-of-the-heavyweights-infographic), 74 trillion emails are sent each year, a mind boggling number when compared to the 8 trillion texts that are sent. Yet, the statistics on which are opened don’t correspond to the volumes. Read on to find out which are the better reminders for pet grooming appointments for your customers.

## Text Message Appointment Reminders versus Email reminders

Continuing with the statistics of the experts, of all those emails only 20% ever get opened. However, SMS open rates are a whopping 98%, opened within less than 90 seconds. Response rates to emails are also minimal, only reaching 6%, with SMS response rates reaching 45%. [Marketing research](https://www.jeeves.plus/why-sms-texting) has shown that 60% of consumers have a positive impression of companies that contact them via text message and they are an effective way for companies to communicate with their customers.

With metrics like these it’s obvious that text messaging is far more effective than email, but you may be wondering why.

Emails cannot be checked frequently, especially if your clients are at work or busy driving around. They often also get lost in the volumes of emails that people get in a day, and often also end up in the spam section, where people hardly ever venture. Many people are wary of opening emails from a source that they are not familiar with in case it contains malware through its links. Often emails are not received as instantly as SMS because they are dependent on a server.

Text messages are brief and to-the point and customers don’t have to wade through other information. From the moment that the sender presses the “send” button, the recipient instantly receives the SMS and can see it on their screens. Besides being a useful tool to use as a reminder for your pet grooming clients, SMS is an invaluable marketing tool and is a more intimate way to interact with clients. SMSs appear on the screen of cellphones and their content can be discreetly scanned in a matter of a few seconds, this can be done at any moment during their busy day and from wherever they are. SMS allow customers to respond instantly if necessary.

If you want to effectively send out appointment reminders to reduce “no shows” then you must use Groomsoft’s  Text Message Appointment Reminders to instantly reach your customers, guaranteeing that they will be read by them in real time.

## About Groomsoft Text Message Appointment Reminders

Text message appointment reminders can be sent once or twice prior to each appointment based upon your settings.

The first reminder will show all the pertinent details of the appointment and ask your customer to confirm by replying Yes. The second reminder will show all the pertinent details of the appointment and if the customer has already confirmed their appointment, they won’t be asked to confirm again. If your customer has not confirmed the first reminder, the second reminder will ask them to confirm.

You set how many days or weeks prior to an appointment you would like one or both of the appointment reminders to go out based upon your pet grooming business needs. Text Message Appointment Reminder [Settings](https://blog.groomsoft.com/reducing-grooming-no-shows-with-text-message-appointment-reminders/#setup) are shown below.

## Confirming appointments via Text Message

A customer can confirm their text message appointment reminder by replying Yes or if your business is in Canada, customers can reply Oui.

![](https://d13ddrtjxhzwjl.cloudfront.net/wp-content/uploads/2019/10/sms-appointment-reminder-replying-yes.png)

Once your customer replies, the appointment status will change to “Confirmed via SMS” so that you know your customer has confirmed.

![](https://d13ddrtjxhzwjl.cloudfront.net/wp-content/uploads/2019/10/Confirmed-via-SMS-appointment-status-1024x630.jpg)

Groomers have told us that the text messaging reminders virtually eliminate their no shows. Is it any wonder with open rates as high as 98%?

## How to set up Text Message Appointment Reminders in Groomsoft

Go to the Settings menu option and choose Calendar Settings.

![](https://d13ddrtjxhzwjl.cloudfront.net/wp-content/uploads/2019/10/Settings-Menu-1024x576.jpg)

Click on the Appointment Reminders link.

![](https://d13ddrtjxhzwjl.cloudfront.net/wp-content/uploads/2019/10/Appointment-reminders-link-1024x650.jpg)

Set the “Send SMS appointment reminders” option to Yes.

![](https://d13ddrtjxhzwjl.cloudfront.net/wp-content/uploads/2019/10/Set-SMS-reminders-to-Yes-1024x347.jpg)

If you want to send Text messages to your customers from Groomsoft or answer their text messages, set “Send SMS via Groomsoft Messenger” to Yes.

![](https://d13ddrtjxhzwjl.cloudfront.net/wp-content/uploads/2019/10/Set-GS-Messenger-to-Yes.jpg)

Groomsoft can remind your customers twice prior to an appointment. Use the “When to remind – 1st reminder” to set when the 1st reminder should be sent and if you wish to send a second reminder set the value of “When to remind – 2nd reminder”.

![](https://d13ddrtjxhzwjl.cloudfront.net/wp-content/uploads/2019/10/Set-1st-reminder-to-1-week-1024x347.jpg)

For instance, you may want to set the first Text Message Appointment Reminder at 1 week and the 2nd at 2 days prior. The choice is yours!

![](https://d13ddrtjxhzwjl.cloudfront.net/wp-content/uploads/2019/10/Set-2nd-reminder-to-2-days.jpg)

The “SMS Reminder Message” field is used to add additional text onto the end of default Text Message Appointment Reminder sent by Groomsoft. You can ad
